finalists.why: This candidate has the strongest evidence for it, with a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation and a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein, and no evidence against it.

finalists.label: Renal Cell Carcinoma
finalists.unexplained: the presence of abdominal and pelvic pain
finalists.why: This candidate has the most comprehensive evidence for it, including a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation, visible vessels extending into the renal cortex, and a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein, with no evidence against it.

finalists.label: Renal Vein Thrombosis
finalists.unexplained: the right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation and visible vessels extending into the renal cortex
finalists.why: This candidate has some evidence for it, with a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein, although it does not account for the right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation.

finalists.label: Myocarditis
finalists.unexplained: the exact cause of the myocarditis and its relation to the recent surgery
finalists.why: The evidence of moderate chronically active myocarditis with diffuse interstitial remodelling carried this nomination inside the group

finalists.label: Cardiomyopathy
finalists.unexplained: the underlying mechanism leading to cardiomyopathy
finalists.why: The specific finding of severely impaired left ventricular systolic function supported this candidate

finalists.label: Cardiogenic Shock
finalists.unexplained: the specific events or conditions that triggered the cardiogenic shock
finalists.why: The direct mention of severe cardiogenic shock with multiorgan failure of unknown cause made this candidate the most fitting

finalists.label: Retroperitoneal fibrosis
finalists.unexplained: The patient's weight loss and epigastric pain
finalists.why: The evidence of a confluent retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass encasing surrounding vessels and bilateral hydronephrosis with extrinsic compression and medial deviation of the ureters strongly supports this candidate.

finalists.label: Malignancy
finalists.unexplained: The absence of fever, chills, or other infectious symptoms
finalists.why: The finding of a confluent retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass encasing surrounding vessels and a significant increase in creatinine level suggests a malignant process.

finalists.label: Sarcoidosis
finalists.unexplained: The patient's hypertension and COPD, which are not directly related to sarcoidosis
finalists.why: The presence of a confluent retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass and bilateral hydronephrosis with extrinsic compression and medial deviation of the ureters could be explained by sarcoidosis, although it is less common.

support_spans: Serum toxoplasma IgG was elevated
CSF studies showed 48 cells/µL (97% lymphocytes) with positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii (286 copies/mL)
Histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites
concepts.why: Toxoplasmosis is a common opportunistic infection in HIV-positive patients and the patient's symptoms and test results are consistent with this diagnosis.

support_spans: HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL
fever to 39.6 °C
a 1-day history of productive cough
Chest radiograph showed a new left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence
concepts.why: Pneumocystis pneumonia is a common opportunistic infection in HIV-positive patients with low CD4 counts and the patient's respiratory symptoms are consistent with this diagnosis.

contradict_spans: Histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites
support_spans: MRI of the brain demonstrated a 2.7-cm ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with mass effect
HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL
concepts.why: Cerebral lymphoma is a possible diagnosis in HIV-positive patients with mass lesions in the brain, but the histopathologic examination revealed Toxoplasma gondii infection.
